text:
Taylor Kim: hey all, first week here! trying to get kubectl working but running into a weird perms/auth mix. hoping someone can point me in the right direction :wave:

Taylor Kim: steps I did: downloaded company kubeconfig to ~/work/onboard/onboard.yaml, merged with my ~/.kube/config, then ran `kubectl get pods -n onboard-taylor` and got `error: exec plugin data is invalid` followed by `x509: certificate signed by unknown authority`. Also I had to sudo once because mv wanted permission. 😬

Taylor Kim: my merged file shows a user with an exec plugin:```
users:
- name: taylor.kim@company
  user:
    exec:
      apiVersion: client.authentication.k8s.io/v1beta1
      command: company-auth
      args: ["get-token", "--format=kubeconfig"]
```

DevEx Bot: welcome Taylor! :tada: A couple of things to check quickly:
• `exec plugin data is invalid` often happens if the auth binary is missing or not executable in your PATH. Is `company-auth` installed and runnable? Try `company-auth --version`.
• `x509` usually means the kubeconfig references a CA file path that doesn't exist on your machine. Use `certificate-authority-data` (base64) instead of `certificate-authority` path in merged files.
• try not to use sudo when editing/moving kubeconfigs; you can end up owning ~/.kube/config as root which breaks the extension. Run `sudo chown $(whoami) ~/.kube/config` if that happened.

Priya Desai: +1 to DevEx Bot. Also check that `company-auth` returns JSON the exec plugin expects. You can run the plugin manually to debug:```
company-auth get-token --format=kubeconfig | jq '.'
```
It should output a valid credential response. If it returns an HTML login page (happened to me once when a proxy blocked auth), kubectl will choke with that exec error.

Taylor Kim: running `company-auth --version` says it's not found. I must have skipped the install step in the onboarding guide. Where do I get it?

Platform Eng: Hey Taylor 12: we ship `company-auth` in the onboarding bundle and also via homebrew for mac/linux. Quick install: `brew tap redwood/inference && brew install company-auth` or grab the binary from our internal downloads at `https://downloads.company.internal/onboard/company-auth-1.2.0.tar.gz`. After install, ensure `~/.local/bin` or `/usr/local/bin` is in PATH.

Platform Eng: if you prefer not to install, you can exchange tokens via the web UI and temporarily replace the user entry with a static `token: <redacted>` for testing, but don't commit that to config.

Taylor Kim: installed company-auth via brew, ran `company-auth get-token --format=kubeconfig` and it printed JSON. Re-ran `kubectl get pods -n onboard-taylor` and now the exec error is gone. Still seeing `x509: certificate signed by unknown authority` though.

DevEx Bot: good progress. For the TLS issue, run `kubectl config view --raw --minify` to inspect the cluster entry your current context points to. If the cluster has `certificate-authority: /some/path/ca.pem`, that path might be valid only on the VM that generated the kubeconfig. Convert it to data with:```
base64 -w0 /path/to/ca.pem  # on linux
base64 /path/to/ca.pem | tr -d '
'  # on mac
```
then replace `certificate-authority` with `certificate-authority-data: <base64>` (backup config first). Alternatively, use the onboard file directly with `kubectl --kubeconfig=~/work/onboard/onboard.yaml get ns` to avoid merge issues.

Taylor Kim: aha, my merged config had `certificate-authority: /root/.certs/onboard/ca.pem` because I accidentally did the `mv` with sudo earlier. chown fixed the file owner but the path still points to /root. I updated the cluster entry to include certificate-authority-data from the onboarding zip and retried — now I can list namespaces! :relieved:

Taylor Kim: next snag — I can list but `kubectl describe pod somepod` returns `forbidden: User "system:serviceaccount:onboard-taylor:default" cannot get resource "pods"` even though my context user is `taylor.kim@company`. Why is it using a serviceaccount?

Priya Desai: that usually means your kubeconfig's user mapping is wrong or minikube leftover context is in effect. Run `kubectl config current-context` and `kubectl config view --minify -o jsonpath='{.users[0].name}'` to confirm the user on the active context. Also `kubectl auth can-i get pods --as system:serviceaccount:onboard-taylor:default` will show serviceaccount rights. If the active context is correct but server-side is mapping you to a serviceaccount, check if you're hitting a different cluster than you think (minikube) or if a webhook is impersonating.

Taylor Kim: current-context is `onboard-taylor@dev`, user shows `taylor.kim@company`. Weird. But when I `kubectl --kubeconfig=~/work/onboard/onboard.yaml describe pod somepod` it works (my user has access). So seems like the merged config is still pointing `server:` to a different cluster (maybe a local docker-desktop) for that context name.

Platform Eng: yup that explains it. When you merge, contexts with the same name can get reordered or point at a different cluster entry. Recommendation: give unique context names before merging, e.g.:```
kubectl config rename-context dev@cluster dev-onboard
kubectl config rename-context minikube minikube-local
```
Then flatten and inspect. Or keep company kubeconfig separate until you finish.

Taylor Kim: thanks, I renamed contexts and now `kubectl` hits the right cluster and my user perms are applied. Last question: because I used sudo earlier my `~/.kube/config` was owned by root for a bit. I chowned it back but should I worry about other files in ~/.kube?

DevEx Bot: check file ownership & perms in `~/.kube`: `ls -la ~/.kube`. Typical perms: files 600 owned by you, dir 700. If you used sudo to create directories, run `sudo chown -R $(whoami):$(id -gn) ~/.kube`. Don't run kubectl as root. Also add a note to docs: "do not use sudo when moving kubeconfig" — common trap.

Onboarding Bot: congrats Taylor 17: I added you to `eng-onboarding` group so your access is permanent. If you need Role changes in `onboard-taylor`, ping here. Welcome to Redwood Inference! :tada:

Taylor Kim: this thread saved my morning — thanks everyone. I'll send a tiny PR to DevEx about the sudo/ownership gotcha and a snippet showing how to rename contexts before merging. :raised_hands:
